name: carroll-diagram
title: Carroll diagram
tagline: Carroll sort grid (2×2, or 2×3 with a categorical axis): items placed into cells derived from two yes/no or numeric-rule properties; cells occlude/highlight, counts derived.
description: A Carroll diagram: a sort grid whose columns are the categories of one property and rows the categories of another, with each item placed in its cell. You write the items — each a label, an optional numeric value, and optional attribute tags — and the two properties to sort by (property 1 = columns, property 2 = rows), each a predicate: an attribute tag (matches an item's tags) or a numeric rule (even, odd, multiple of k, greater than / less than / at least / at most / between). The cell every item belongs to is derived by evaluating those predicates; the negative category headers ("Not even"), the per-cell counts and the grid sizing are all computed too. There is no way to author an item's position, so the diagram cannot mis-sort. A yes/no property gives a 2×2; a categorical property (its own list of `categories`) gives a 2×3. Occlude a cell to ask "what goes here?" (the count blanks with it, no leak); colour tags tint the chips their real colour for colour sorts. For the overlapping-circle form of the same sorting (a Venn / sorting circles), use probability/venn — this model is the grid.
whenToUse: Reach for this to sort or classify a set of numbers or shapes by two yes/no questions at once — the primary (KS1/KS2) Carroll-diagram work and lower-secondary two-way sorting. Author the semantics only — list the `items` (label + `value` for number sorts, + `attrs` tags for shape/colour/feature sorts) and the two `properties` (each a `tag` or a numeric `rule`); every item is then placed for you. Property 1 makes the columns, property 2 the rows; a yes/no property gives a 2×2 (its negative "Not even" header is derived — override with `notLabel`), a categorical property (`categories`) gives a 2×3 (e.g. a colour or size-band axis). Common configurations: worked — list everything and let it sort (turn on `show.counts` for "how many are even and a multiple of 3?"); blank answer space — `show.items:false` draws the empty headed grid for pupils to fill in ("sort these into the diagram"); occluded question — occlude a cell (`cells:[{col,row,occlude:true}]`) to ask "what goes in this cell?"; single-axis — give one property for a simple two-column (odd/even) split. Colour sorts: tag items "red"/"blue"/… and the chips render in that colour. Staged builds read well: open on the empty headed grid (`show.items:false`, or every cell `blank`) and reveal one cell per stage; or pose an occluded cell and reveal the answer. The grid handles large sets — cells grow to hold many chips. Cross-block convention: keep the same items, properties and headers across a lesson so pupils track one diagram — change only what is hidden, blanked or highlighted. Use probability/venn instead when the sorting wants overlapping circles (a Venn). Synonyms a teacher might use: Carroll diagram, sorting diagram, sort, classify, classification, two-way sort, sorting grid, attribute, property, criteria, odd and even, multiples, factors, shape sort, colour sort.

rule.description: A numeric predicate evaluated on the item's `value`. An item with no `value` fails every numeric rule (so it lands in the "not" category).

kind.description: even / odd: value parity. multipleOf: value is a multiple of `k`. greaterThan / lessThan / atLeast / atMost: compare value to `k` (atLeast = ≥, atMost = ≤). between: min ≤ value ≤ max (inclusive).

k.description: The comparison number for multipleOf / greaterThan / lessThan / atLeast / atMost. Ignored by even/odd/between.

items.description: One thing to be sorted, drawn as a labelled chip. Its placement is DERIVED from its `value` / `attrs` against the two properties — you never say which cell it goes in.

label.description: The text on the chip — the item being sorted ("12", "cat", "red triangle"). If omitted, the `value` is shown.

value.description: A number used by numeric `rule` predicates (even, multipleOf, greaterThan, …). Omit for purely categorical items (sorted only by `attrs`).

attrs.description: Attribute tags this item HAS, tested by `tag` predicates — ["red", "triangle", "has-right-angle"]. A recognised colour tag (red, blue, green, yellow, orange, purple, pink) also TINTS the chip its real colour (a sanctioned manipulative-colour convention for colour sorts).

highlight.description: Amber this chip — draw the eye to one item. Default false.

occlude.description: Hide this single chip's label as "?" while still placing it. Rare; usually you occlude a whole cell instead. Default false.

items.description: The things to sort, each drawn as a chip. Placement is derived from each item's `value` / `attrs` against the properties — you never place a chip. Set `show.items:false` for a blank answer space (the items still define the diagram's shape).

One sorting property / axis. Property 1 is the COLUMNS, property 2 is the ROWS. A plain property is YES/NO (its predicate is the positive category, e.g. "Even", and the negative "Not even" is derived); add `categories` to make the axis categorical (a 2×3). Give exactly one of `tag`, `rule` or `categories`.

name.description: The positive-category header — "Even", "Multiple of 3", "Red", "Has a right angle".

tag.description: Categorical predicate: an item satisfies this property when its `attrs` list includes this tag (e.g. tag "red" matches an item with attrs ["red", …]). Use for shape/colour/feature sorts.

notLabel.description: Override the derived NEGATIVE category header (default "Not " + a lowercased name, e.g. "Not even"). e.g. "Odd" for an Even property, or "Not a multiple of 3".

items.description: One column or row of a CATEGORICAL axis (use this to make a 2×3, e.g. a colour axis Red | Blue | Green). Each category is a label plus its own predicate; an item is placed in the FIRST category it satisfies. Categories should be mutually exclusive and cover every item — an item matching none lands in a derived "Other" column/row that only appears when something falls there.

label.description: The column/row header for this category — "Red", "Blue".

tag.description: Categorical predicate: an item is in this category when its `attrs` include this tag.

categories.description: Make this axis CATEGORICAL instead of yes/no — one column (property 1) or row (property 2) per category, e.g. a colour axis [{label:"Red",tag:"red"},{label:"Blue",tag:"blue"},{label:"Green",tag:"green"}] gives a 2×3.

properties.description: The two sorting criteria. Property 1 = the COLUMNS axis, property 2 = the ROWS axis. Give ONE property for a single-axis (2-column) split, or two for a full grid. Each is a `tag` or a numeric `rule`; an axis may be made categorical with `categories`.

items.description: Mark one cell (occlude / highlight / blank it). Address by 1-based column and row in the RENDERED order: a yes/no axis is positive-then-negative (Even = col 1, Not even = col 2); a categorical axis follows the authored category order, with any derived "Other" last.

col.description: Column index from 1 (property 1, the columns axis).

row.description: Row index from 1 (property 2, the rows axis).

occlude.description: Render this cell's contents (and its count) as "?" — the "what goes here?" hook. Default false.

highlight.description: Amber-tint this cell — emphasis / the answer cell. Default false.

blank.description: Render this cell empty (no chips) — an unfilled cell for a staged build. Different from occlude: "?" poses a question, blank poses nothing yet. Default false.

cells.description: Per-cell occlude / highlight / blank marks (the cells always exist and are filled automatically; list one here only to mark it).

items.description: Draw the item chips. false renders the empty headed grid — a blank answer space for "sort these into the diagram". Default true.

counts.description: Show the derived count of items in each cell (a small tally). Occluded cells show "?" for the count too. Default false.

frame.description: Draw the grid outline. Default true.

header.description: Optional short title centred above the figure; the top padding grows to clear it.

caption.description: Optional line centred below the figure, e.g. a short context note. Never the question or an instruction: that wording is the block's text.
